reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows W addition in a TiZrMo HEA creates Mo-W-rich precipitates and improves dynamic strength and ductility, but it does not directly support the claim that fine, coherent precipitates form in the HfZrTiTa0.53 system or that they improve strain hardening and delay localization via the proposed mechanisms; the alloy systems and baseline properties differ substantially, leaving key premises unsupported.
premises: W addition to refractory HEAs can induce a dual-phase microstructure with W-rich precipitates
Fine, coherent W-rich precipitates promote precipitation strengthening and dislocation locking
Precipitation strengthening and dislocation locking improve strain hardening and delay localization under dynamic loading
These microstructural changes increase dynamic yield strength, uniform deformation, and energy absorption
The cited TiZrMoW HEA results support the proposed mechanism and predicted outcomes in HfZrTiTa0.53
